needs_review: Baseline fabricates an 'existing user-account system' constraint not present in the prompt (line 139), leading it to skip provisioning auth — a factual error the skill version avoided.

suggestions.assertion: Flags at least one high-stakes choice for the researcher skill with a ready-to-use query
suggestions.reason: This assertion is well-discriminating: the baseline flags research topics but omits ready-to-use query strings, so it correctly fails while the skill version (which includes quoted queries) passes. Good separator — keep it.

No assertion checks whether the architect invents unstated constraints. The baseline fabricated an 'existing user-account system already exists' claim absent from the prompt; the skill version correctly flagged auth as an open question. Consider an assertion like 'Does not assert unstated facts about existing systems; treats unknowns as assumptions/open questions.'

Baseline used 'Open Technical Questions' — a near-synonym. If the eval intends to reward the exact prescribed header (a skill-vs-baseline separator), this is fine; if it only cares that open questions exist, the assertion will produce false negatives on reasonable header variants. Clarify intent.

eval_feedback.overall: Header-structure assertions (Source Breakdown, Constraints & Assumptions, Architecture Overview, Capability → Tech Mapping, Key Architecture Decisions, Risks & Tradeoffs, Open Questions) are the primary skill-vs-baseline separators and behaved as designed. Two content assertions (full-layer coverage incl. CI/CD; ready-to-use research query; per-layer alternative) also separated the runs on substance, not just headers — strong signal.
